purpose: Calibrate and validate the sky130 area model (DEVICE_MODELS.MEASURE_NETLIST_AREA / LOAD_CELL_AREAS, SYN.ESTIMATE_DESIGN_AREA) against latchup.app's own reported total cell area for the same radix-2 divider used to select the delay model's production recipe.

definitional_area_sum_check.description: Sum of this repo's own vendored liberty area: attribute over latchup's OWN synth.v cell histogram (regex-extracted directly from their post-early-flatten mapped Verilog, no PipelineC build involved on either side). Establishes that 'area = sum of per-cell liberty area over a mapped netlist' is definitionally what latchup reports, independent of any recipe-reproduction question below.

reproduced_builds.description: Each design rebuilt from latchup's own solution.py (CLK_RATE_MHZ/PART unchanged) via this repo's pypelinec, `--syn_tool sky130 --no_hier_syn --no_sweep` (latchup's own build flags, confirmed by their pypelinec.log). Slice count is whatever --no_sweep's planner guess produces at that target MHz -- NOT forced to match latchup's reported slice count.

34cycles_161mhz.slice_mismatch_note: latchup reports 33 slices at this target; this repo's current --no_sweep planner guess is 65. Not an area-model question -- see planner_drift_note below.

65cycles_173mhz.slice_mismatch_note: latchup reports 64 slices at this target; this repo's current --no_sweep planner guess is 97. Not an area-model question -- see planner_drift_note below.

planner_drift_note: docs/DEVICE_MODELS_DESIGN.md's 2026-08-20 recipe-selection entry recorded all 4 designs reproducing latchup's exact top-entity hash under this same --no_sweep --no_hier_syn invocation. Rebuilt one week later (2026-08-27, commit 9fb4be5) against the same solution.py sources, only the 17- and 33-stage designs still reproduce latchup's slice count; the 34- and 65-stage targets now produce 65 and 97 slices instead of 33 and 64. This is planner-guess drift in --no_sweep's pipelining heuristics since 2026-08-20 (see recent 'autopipeline sweep improvements' commits), unrelated to this area model -- recorded here rather than silently worked around. The measured/estimated area at the ACTUAL slices built is still reported above for those two designs; only their comparison against latchup's reported number is suppressed (error_pct: null) since they are no longer the same design point.

interpretation.measured_area: DEVICE_MODELS.MEASURE_NETLIST_AREA on a real whole-design mapped netlist (mode 2, or mode 1's forced per-leaf remeasure) is highly accurate: 2.87% MAE against latchup's real reported area on the two cleanly-reproduced designs, consistent with the definitional check above (0.0001% MAE) once recipe/histogram fidelity is accounted for -- matching the delay model's own already-documented ~5% engine residual in magnitude.
interpretation.estimated_area: SYN.ESTIMATE_DESIGN_AREA (sum of isolated per-leaf cached areas plus PipelineC's own FF count, no synthesis) overshoots real measured area by 270-410% on every design here, and BOTH terms overshoot, not just the combinational one: the combinational term (fixed at 464724.3 um2, all 4 static leaf entities) runs 2.7-3.6x over real measured combinational area (172667/128072 um2 at 16/32 slices), which mirrors an ALREADY DOCUMENTED limitation of the isolated delay estimate on this exact design family (docs/DEVICE_MODELS_DESIGN.md: '--no_hier_syn sums isolated per-leaf delays, which runs high on a mux chain specifically', ~2.5x for delay) -- this divider unrolls the same MINUS/MUX operators dozens of times, and real synthesis's cross-instance optimization shares/dedupes across them in a way an isolated per-leaf sum cannot see. The sequential term is WORSE, not better: estimated_n_ffs overshoots real measured_n_sequential_cells by 5.7-5.9x (10589 vs 1853 at 16 slices, 20977 vs 3584 at 32 slices) -- GET_REGISTERS_ESTIMATE_TEXT_AND_FFS counts every declared pipeline-register bit before any of yosys's own FF-level optimization (constant/dead-bit elimination, retiming), which apparently removes the large majority of them on this design. Per-FF area itself is exact by construction (estimated_sequential_area_um2 / estimated_n_ffs == measured_sequential_area_um2 / measured_n_sequential_cells == GET_SEQUENTIAL_CELL_AREA's 48.84 um2), so 100% of the sequential term's error is in the FF COUNT, not the per-FF cost. Net: the cheap estimate is not a usable absolute area predictor on a design with this much structural repetition in either operators or registers -- at best a same-design, same-direction relative signal (more slices still costs more of both terms) until AUTOFSM-side work (out of scope here) closes the FF-count gap.
